title: Fate's Backlash
next_chapter_hook: Su Qingyao gazed at the unhealing crack, finally realizing—to share Chen Ji's Heavenly Fate backlash, the price she would need to pay was far more than just cultivation.

text.content: The moment three distinctly different powers extended their olive branches to him, Chen Ji knew he had touched the edge of the chessboard that shrouded the world. Yet before he could ponder further, a soul-tearing agony exploded from his Brow Center—the Tianji Record Fragment was quivering, the beginning of the backlash from the power of writing fate.

dialogue.content: Cough...

text.content: Chen Ji knelt on one knee, veins bulging on his forehead, blood dripping from his nostrils onto the cold Blue Stone, spreading into startling red plum blossoms. The Tianji Record Fragment suspended in his Mental Sea was now disintegrating at a visible speed—golden text distorting, black cracks spreading like spiderwebs, as if some invisible existence was tearing it apart inch by inch from within.

dialogue.content: "Too hasty." Mo Xiansheng's aged voice echoed from deep within the Fragment, carrying helplessness and heartache, "I told you, before Heavenly Fate Value is full, do not lightly activate fate writing... What exactly did you write with that stroke?"

text.content: Chen Ji forced his lips into a smile, the expression carrying self-mockery. What did he write? He wrote the turning point of fate for one of the three great sects, the future trajectory of a key figure who should have died. He thought the meager three hours of foresight was enough to support his pen in rewriting—yet he didn't realize, this single stroke had directly drained a full thirty percent of his Heavenly Fate reserves.

dialogue.content: "Merely... changed one person's death date." Chen Ji forced himself to stand, his voice hoarse and barely coherent, "Didn't expect the backlash to come so... fast." Before the words finished, another violent coughing fit struck, bringing up a mouthful of blood and phlegm mixed black and red.

text.content: The Tianji Record Fragment in his Mental Sea shuddered violently, the cracks expanding by another three fen. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul fluctuated intensely, his voice carrying a rare urgency: "Heavenly Fate Value is draining frantically! If this continues, in less than three ke, you will—" He paused, as if unwilling to speak the ending.

dialogue.content: "Die?" Chen Ji laughed instead, the smile pale as paper yet carrying a chilling calm, "I've survived even shorter lives than this. Rather, Mo Xiansheng... this appearance more frantic than mine makes me curious, what exactly did this stroke of mine touch?"

choice.prompt: Facing the dual crisis of Tianji Record Fragment disintegration and Heavenly Fate Value drainage, Chen Ji must make a choice—

text.content: Chen Ji clenched his teeth, what seeped from his temples was no longer clear if sweat or blood. Using the endurance he had honed through twenty years of being atrash, he forcibly suppressed the rampaging spiritual energy back into his meridians—the cost: every inch of skin felt like being gnawed by ten thousand ants, every bone screaming.

dialogue.content: "...I've noted it down." He murmured in a voice only he could hear, "Once I find out who's behind this scheme, I'll pay it back stroke by stroke."

choices.visible_reward: Obtain a method to temporarily suppress the backlash

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng was silent for a moment, his remnant soul dimming slightly: "There is a method, but the cost... never mind, listen carefully—"

text.content: A obscure guiding method transmitted into Chen Ji's Mental Sea, precisely the "Reverse Fate Preservation Technique" Mo Xiansheng had incidentally learned in his youth. This technique could temporarily seal one's perception in exchange for temporary stability of spiritual energy and Heavenly Fate—the cost: during its use, he would become completely鱼肉.

choices.visible_reward: Preserve most of the Heavenly Fate, maintaining combat power

text.content: Chen Ji drew out an exquisite 'Soul Calming Jade' from his storage bag—this was one of the trump cards he had accumulated over years of scheming, originally meant for crucial life-saving moments. Now, to cut his losses, he had to reluctantly crush it, turning it into a medium to bear the backlash.

dialogue.content: 'What a pity.' He watched the Soul Calming Jade turn to ashes, murmuring softly, 'But anything that can be solved with money isn't a real problem.' His tone was calm, as if he had merely lost an insignificant common object.

text.content: Just as Chen Ji was weighing the pros and cons, hurried footsteps suddenly sounded outside his cave dwelling. He knew those footsteps too well—they were the distinctive gait of the Tianqing Sect's Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, steady yet carrying a subtle, hard-to-detect anxiety. The next moment, the barrier was violently shattered, and a white-robed figure swept in like a startled swan.

dialogue.content: 'Chen Ji!' Su Qingyao's voice lacked its usual icy composure, instead carrying an overwhelming wave of panic. She immediately noticed Chen Ji's disheveled state—his face deathly pale, blood still wet at the corner of his mouth, spiritual energy swirling chaotically around him like a dissipating storm. She rushed forward, steadying his trembling form: 'You... what happened to you?'

text.content: Chen Ji instinctively wanted to push her away, but his heart seized when he glimpsed her expression. Those typically cold, assessing eyes now blazed with undisguised concern and heartache. This realization caused a dull ache somewhere in his chest—whether it was the remnant wave of backlash, or something else entirely.

dialogue.content: 'Why all the fuss, Senior Sister Su?' He forced a sickly smile, his voice deliberately light, 'Just a minor cultivation mishap—nothing serious. But Senior Sister barging into my cave at midnight... I wonder what people would say if they found out...'

'Shut up!' Su Qingyao rarel cut him off sharply, her voice trembling, 'Do you think I'm blind? Your spiritual energy is in such chaos—this is far from a simple cultivation accident. What forbidden technique did you use?' Her hand pressed against his pulse, probing with spiritual sense, only to be violently repelled by the surging karmic force: 'This is... karmic backlash?'

text.content: Chen Ji offered no answer, simply turning his face slightly away to evade her burning gaze. Silence itself was an answer. Su Qingyao's breath quickened as she stared fixedly at his pale, nearly translucent profile, her heart churning with indescribable emotions—anger, heartache, and a helpless sense of defeat. This 'waste' she had investigated for years harbored secrets far deeper and more dangerous than she ever imagined.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao has already sensed the signs of karmic backlash. How should Chen Ji respond?

dialogue.content: '...I can see some things.' Chen Ji finally spoke, his voice hoarse. 'Events within three hours. But each use requires a price.' He paused. 'This time, the price was rather steep.'

Su Qingyao's pupils contracted sharply. Foreseeing the future—this was a domain that only supreme experts could touch, yet this servant disciple竟然... She took a deep breath, suppressing the surging tide within her: 'So your 'waste' persona was a lie from the very beginning.'

dialogue.content: 「Su Senior Sister is overthinking.」 Chen Ji lowered his gaze, hiding all emotions in the shadows. 「They're merely old injuries; they'll pass with time. With Senior Sister's busy affairs, why bother concerning yourself with a mere servant?」

Su Qingyao's hand froze mid-air, the light in her eyes fading bit by bit. Suddenly she felt this person was both familiar and unfamiliar—clearly close at hand, yet as if separated by countless mountains and seas. She bit her lip, ultimately choosing not to press further, only leaving behind these words before turning away: 「Chen Ji, I'll remember you.」

choices.description: Using the foresight ability to show Su Qingyao dangers she herself wasn't aware of, steering the conversation in another direction
choices.visible_reward: Successfully shifting Su Qingyao's attention, gaining control of the conversation
choices.risk_hint: May deepen Su Qingyao's suspicion, laying hidden troubles for the future

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly raised his head, his usually dull eyes now sharp as a blade: 「Su Senior Sister, before I tell you the reason, aren't you curious... why you happened to arrive at this precise moment?」

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao froze mid-step. Chen Ji pulled out a shattered jade talisman from his chest—this was a key item from a vision he'd foreseen three days prior: 「In three days, a black-clad figure will break into the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow's quarters. And tonight, I happened to see that person's face.」

text.content: At this moment, a cold voice seeped from the void, carrying a playful smile: 「Oh, so this is the 'Trash Senior Fellow' of Tianqing Sect who made a name across three sects? Indeed interesting.」 Su Qingyao's expression changed dramatically, her sword flashing as she protected Chen Ji: 「Who goes there!」 A wisp of black mist condensed from the shadows, forming the silhouette of a graceful woman—the Demonic Path Holy Maiden Ye Qing had actually infiltrated Tianqing Sect's territory undetected.

dialogue.content: Ye Qing's gaze swept over Chen Ji's disheveled appearance, her brow slightly raised: 「Fate's backlash? Seems you're more impatient than I imagined.」 She raised her hand, a barrier of demonic energy forming to isolate this place's aura from leaking outward. 「But since we agreed to cooperate, I can't just watch an ally die before my eyes.」

Su Qingyao's sword tip pointed directly at Ye Qing, killing intent凛然 around her: 「Demonic path witch! How dare you infiltrate Tianqing Sect!」 Though unaware of what transaction existed between Chen Ji and Ye Qing, the identity of the Demonic Path Holy Maiden itself was enough to make her vigilant. Sword intent and demonic energy confronted each other, causing the cave's temperature to plummet.

text.content: Chen Ji forced himself to stand, reaching out to press Su Qingyao's sword-wielding wrist—the touch was ice-cold, causing him to furrow his brow slightly: 「Su Senior Sister, she's not an enemy.」 His voice was soft, yet carried undeniable certainty. Su Qingyao looked at him in confusion, but Chen Ji shook his head gently, a complex emotion flickering in his eyes.

dialogue.content: 「Since Ye Holy Maiden is here, I presume it's not just to watch my humiliation.」 Chen Ji gazed at the shadowy figure, a faint smile curving his lips. 「Go on, what have you sensed?」

Ye Qing laughed lightly, her form drifting to Chen Ji's side, her voice dropping: 「My demonic path mist has sensed something anomalous—someone is using some power beyond the norm to peer into this place. And the source of that power...」 She paused. 「Has the same origin as your Tianji Record.」

These three forces that should have repelled each other instead formed a perfect closed loop through unexpected synergy, sealing all anomalous auras completely within.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao sheathed her sword, her gaze complex as it swept across Ye Qing before ultimately fixing on Chen Ji: 「So, the Demonic Path Holy Maiden... is your ally?」 Her voice carried an indefinable nuance. 「You've truly given me reason to reconsider.」

dialogue.content: "Since avoidance is impossible, better to take the initiative." Chen Ji suddenly released his suppression on the Tianji Record, allowing that unique aura to surge out like a tide. He wanted to see how those chess players hiding in the shadows would react.

Ye Qing's eyes lit up, her gaze toward Chen Ji gaining more appreciation: "Indeed a madman. But... I like it." The demonic mist around her not only didn't recede, but became even denser, enveloping Chen Ji's leaking aura, ready to respond to any sudden situations.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji silently called out to Mo Xiansheng in his heart, but the response made his heart sink—the elderly remnant soul had faded to near transparency, like a candle guttering in the wind. Yet even so, Mo Xiansheng sighed: "Very well, young man... this old one will help you once more."

text.content: A gentle and ancient power surged from the depths of Chen Ji's Mental Sea, like an invisible hand gently smoothing out the Tianji Record's cracks, isolating that gaze of probing. Yet at this moment, Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul completely dimmed, leaving only faint wisps of consciousness.

The crisis was temporarily resolved, but the atmosphere within the cave dwelling became subtle. Su Qingyao and Ye Qing—two gazes from righteous and demonic paths—intersected on Chen Ji, each harboring their own thoughts. Chen Ji merely sat quietly in place, allowing waves of weakness to assault him, yet his gaze passed through these two people before him, falling toward the distant Void—where something was watching him.

dialogue.content: "Who exactly are you?" Su Qingyao's voice was soft, yet carried an unprecedented seriousness. "Thetrash servant of the Tianqing Sect? The key piece in the secret maneuvering of three major sects? Or..." She paused. "The person who has been arranging the world?"

text.content: Upon hearing this, Chen Ji actually laughed softly. That smile was pale and weary, yet carried a clarity that seemed to see through worldly affairs: "Senior Sister Su, what do you think?" He raised his head, meeting that scrutinizing gaze. "If I said I'm merely an ordinary person who wants to survive... would you believe it?"

Su Qingyao fell silent. She suddenly realized this person before her was far more complex than she'd imagined—beneath his smile lay too many things she couldn't understand, and both his vulnerability and strength made her heart ache. This "trash" she'd investigated for three years was now so unguardedly exposed before her, yet it sparked an impulse within her to protect.

Ye Qing chuckled to the side: "The Inner Disciple Senior Fellow of the Tianqing Sect, the Saint of the Demonic Path's Holy Sect, actually guarding atrash servant together..." She glanced meaningfully at Su Qingyao. "Chen Ji, your connections are far better than I imagined." Chen Ji didn't respond, merely lowering his eyes, allowing exhaustion to overwhelm him.

After an unknown time, Chen Ji suddenly felt weight on his shoulder—a gray cloth robe with a cool fragrance was draped over him. He slightly faltered, raising his head to meet Su Qingyao's turned-away profile, her ear tips faintly flushed: "Don't misunderstand, it's just... your current appearance is too unsightly. If it spread, it would shame the Tianqing Sect." The tone was stiff, but the movements were overly gentle. Ye Qing watched with great interest, her lips curving into a meaningful arc.

Chen Ji gazed at the white garment on his body, suddenly feeling a dull ache somewhere in his chest. The sensation of being cared for—he hadn't experienced it in so long, nearly forgotten. Twenty years oftrash life had long accustomed him to bearing everything alone, to treating everyone as chess pieces in his schemes. Yet at this moment, Su Qingyao's concern was like a soft blade, slowly cutting through his层层包裹的外壳.

dialogue.content: "...Thank you." Chen Ji's voice was very soft, as if afraid to disturb something. He didn't say more, yet in those usually murky eyes, a thin layer of water light now shimmered. This was the first time in twenty years since arriving in this world that he'd shown such vulnerability before others.

text.content: Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul let out a silent sigh in the depths of his Mental Sea. Watching this young person he'd seen grow up, complex emotions stirred within him. Chen Xuan was the same way back then—able to scheme everything, yet when facing those who truly cared for him, he couldn't help but soften. The gears of fate had begun to accelerate turning, and the choices this child would soon face would be more cruel than any before.

As night deepened, the three within the cave dwelling fell into their own contemplation. Chen Ji closed his eyes to regulate his breathing, feeling the chaos within his body gradually settle, yet at a certain moment he abruptly opened his eyes—he saw something. A blurry image flashed through his mind, in which Su Qingyao, her face covered in blood, lay in his arms, repeatedly saying the same words.

"Su Qingyao..." Chen Ji instinctively called her name, his voice carrying a trembling he himself hadn't noticed. Su Qingyao turned at the sound, only to see Chen Ji's complexion was even paler than before, those eyes staring directly at her as if gazing upon some terrifying future. Her heart tightened, and just as she was about to ask, Chen Ji had already turned away, his Adam's apple rolling, swallowing the unfinished words back into his stomach.

Ye Qing keenly sensed the abnormality, her gaze scanning between Chen Ji and Su Qingyao, deep in thought. Yet Su Qingyao seemed to sense something, proactively moving closer to Chen Ji, her hand reaching for his pulse. This time, she didn't use spiritual power to investigate, merely gently resting her fingertips on his wrist, as if confirming something. "What did you see?" Her voice was soft, carrying a trace of indescribable heartache.

Chen Ji opened his mouth, but no words came out about that scene. He merely gripped Su Qingyao's wrist tightly, the force so strong it might leave bruises. The emotions in those eyes were too complex—fear, heartache, and a determination bordering on despair. Su Qingyao didn't pull away; she quietly let him hold her, as if at this moment, she finally understood all the words he had never spoken.

"I won't let that future happen." Chen Ji's voice was hoarse and firm, like an oath. He looked at this woman who had investigated him for three years and now guarded him recklessly, and an unfamiliar emotion surged in his heart—not calculation, not exploitation, but a pure desire to protect her, to keep her forever uninvolved in this chess game.

Su Qingyao gazed at the emotions churning in his eyes, and her heart skipped a beat. She wanted to say something, yet found herself utterly speechless. Just then, Ye Qing suddenly broke the silence: "You'll have plenty of time to be sweet later." Her voice carried a hint of teasing, though something serious flickered in her eyes. "Now, you should see this—" She raised her hand, projecting a ghostly light into the air that formed a blurry image. In the image, a hunched figure stood on a peak outside the Tianqing Sect, gazing toward the cave dwelling from afar.

dialogue.content: "The former Sect Master, Ling Yuan." Ye Qing's voice grew heavy. "He seems to have sensed the anomaly here and is using some secret technique to peep."

text.content: Chen Ji's gaze instantly sharpened to a blade's edge. Ling Yuan—the old Sect Master who sheltered him on the surface but harbored malicious intent beneath. He should have known this man would seize upon any trace of abnormality. At this moment, Su Qingyao's hand remained on his wrist, its warm touch weaving his killing intent and tenderness into a strange, intertwined emotion. He couldn't drag her into this. He couldn't let her become a sacrifice in this chess game.

Su Qingyao sensed his sudden tightened fingers and frowned slightly: "Chen Ji?" She keenly noticed his unusual state. "What are you afraid of?" Chen Ji didn't answer. He slowly released her hand and stood up. His back looked exceptionally lonely in the dim spiritual light, yet also exceptionally resolute. "Nothing." His voice returned to its usual calm. "There are just some things I need to face alone."

Su Qingyao rose abruptly, grabbing his sleeve: "You're going to carry it alone again?" Her voice carried suppressed anger. "Who do you think you are? The backlash of fate, Ling Yuan's surveillance, the enemies lurking in the shadows—can you handle all that alone?" Chen Ji turned to face her. His eyes brimmed with complex emotions that finally dissolved into a sigh: "Su Qingyao, do you know why I became atrash?"

dialogue.content: "Because I didn't want anyone to die because of me." Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet carried the weight of a thousand jun. "I've seen too many futures, and in every one, as long as the people close to me were important enough, they became筹码 for others to threaten me. So I'd rather be atrash, rather be looked down upon by everyone, than... drag you into this."

text.content: Su Qingyao froze. She gazed at this man speaking calmly before her, suddenly realizing he was far more lonely and fragile than she'd imagined. Twenty years—he had spent twenty years disguising himself as atrash, all to protect those around him from dying because of him. How could she not ache for such a person? Her eyes reddened slightly, yet her voice deliberately hardened: "So you plan to die alone and let us feel guilty for a lifetime?"

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji, listen carefully." Su Qingyao took a deep breath, speaking each word deliberately. "From today onward, you are no longer alone. Whether you're scheming across the world or making flawless plans—since I, Su Qingyao, have chosen to stand by your side, I won't back down." Her hand clutched his sleeve tightly, as if making an oath. "If you die, I'll die with you."

text.content: Chen Ji stared at her, his chest feeling as if something had violently struck it. This woman who had investigated him for three years now spoke such words. He wanted to refuse, to say those habitual words of rejection, but when he met her determined gaze, he swallowed all his words. Ye Qing sighed nearby: "Great, another handful to worry about." Though her tone carried teasing, a trace of envy flickered in her eyes—such camaraderie in battle was precisely what she had never possessed.

"...Alright." Chen Ji finally spoke, his voice so hoarse it was nearly unrecognizable. "Then together." Just three short words, yet they seemed to have drained him of all his strength. Upon hearing this, Su Qingyao finally revealed her first genuine smile of the night. That smile was like ice and snow beginning to thaw, leaving Chen Ji momentarily dazed. He suddenly realized the weight this woman held in his life might have long exceeded his expectations.

When had the night sky beyond the cave dwelling begun to pale? Ling Yuan's figure had already vanished from the mountaintop. But Chen Ji knew this was merely the calm before the storm. The backlash of fate had not ended, the surveillance of the Heavenly Eye was like a shadow following him, and the chess player lurking in the darkness was tightening the great net that enveloped the world step by step. Yet now, two people stood beside him—a righteous sect genius and a demonic path saint—three people who should never have crossed paths, now bound together by the threads of fate.

Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul trembled slightly in the depths of his Mental Sea, seemingly transmitting some kind of message. Chen Ji closed his eyes to sense it, and a stream of information flooded into his mind—about the root of fate's backlash, about the possibility of sharing the backlash, about... that blurry scene he hadn't yet revealed. His heart sank violently, though his expression remained undisturbed. Sharing the backlash—if this was true, then Su Qingyao's oath just now might become the final straw to crush her.

Su Qingyao noticed his unusual state and was about to ask, but Chen Ji had already opened his eyes. His gaze fell on her face, carrying a complex emotion she had never seen before—tenderness and sorrow intertwined. "Su Qingyao." He softly called her name, his voice carrying a plea-like quality. "Promise me one thing."

dialogue.content: "If one day I tell you that a choice will harm you—don't promise me." Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet each word was clear. "No matter what reason I give, no matter how resolute I appear... don't believe me." His gaze deeply gazed into her. "Can you do that?"

text.content: Su Qingyao froze. She didn't understand why he would suddenly say such words, but she could feel the weight and despair hidden within them. This man who made flawless plans was now like a child afraid of losing his treasure. She wanted to press for answers, but when she touched the vulnerability in his eyes, all her words transformed into a tight embrace. "I promise you." Her voice came muffled from against his shoulder. "But you must also promise me—don't bear it alone."

Chen Ji felt the warm weight in his arms, and a bitter smile drifted across his lips. He raised his hand, hesitated, then finally gently encircled her waist. This embrace was light, yet seemed to carry twenty years of loneliness and exhaustion. Ye Qing watched quietly nearby, not interrupting. She gazed at the embracing silhouettes, and an indescribable emotion flickered in her eyes—whether envy or emotion, even she couldn't distinguish.

The eastern horizon had begun to show a faint golden hue, and the long night had finally passed. Chen Ji released Su Qingyao and looked at her reddened eyes, an unprecedented emotion surging in his heart. He knew from this moment, he could no longer treat her as an ordinary chess piece. And that blurry future—the scene of Su Qingyao bloodied and collapsed in his arms—he would never let it become reality. Even if it meant wagering everything.

Morning light streamed through the gaps in the cave dwelling, falling upon the three people's faces. Traces of tears still lingered in Su Qingyao's eyes, though her usual determination had returned. Ye Qing's figure flickered in the play of light and shadow, mysterious and dangerous. And Chen Ji—this disciple who had hidden his secrets for twenty years—had finally shed part of his disguise before them. He knew the true storm was just beginning. The backlash of the Tianji Record, Ling Yuan's surveillance, the demonic path's coveting, the Heavenly Eye's scheming—all the chess players were closing in on him. But at this moment, he was no longer alone.

"Let's solve the immediate problem first." Chen Ji gathered his scattered thoughts, his voice regaining its usual composure. "Since Ling Yuan has grown suspicious, he will surely take action next. Su Qingyao, would you mind watching the sect's movements for me? As for the Saint of the demonic path..." He looked toward that shadowy figure. "Any news from the demonic side?" Night was fading, and a new game was just beginning. Chen Ji gazed at the brightening horizon, silently calculating each move ahead. Though the backlash of his Heavenly Fate had been temporarily suppressed, it was like a bomb that could explode at any moment. And all he could do was eliminate every threat before it detonated.

Su Qingyao gazed at him returning to his astute self, her heart churning with mixed emotions. The vulnerable Chen Ji who had seemed like a child moments ago was now merely an illusion; the man before her had transformed back into a flawless strategist. But she knew it was precisely this resilience that made her ache for him even more. She stepped forward, standing shoulder to shoulder with him: "From the day I sensed something was wrong with you, I knew you were no ordinary person." Her voice was soft. "But I never imagined the burden you carried... was even heavier than I could have conceived."

Chen Ji glanced at her, a faint smile curling his lips: "Do you regret it, Su Qingyao?" Su Qingyao snorted coldly: "Regret? I, Su Qingyao, never regret my decisions." Her gaze fell on the not-yet-healed crack in the Tianji Record, deep in thought. "I just feel heartache..." Her voice dropped. "Heartache that you've carried this alone for so long." Chen Ji froze. These two words were like a soft blade, gently cutting through his层层包裹的外壳. He turned his face away, not letting her see his reddening eyes: "You'll get used to it." His voice was somewhat hoarse. "After all, this lifetime... I don't plan to change."

Ye Qing finally couldn't resist speaking: "Alright, alright, starting the sentimental stuff first thing in the morning." She waved her hand to dispel the demonic path mist and stretched lazily. "Chen Ji, your backlash has stabilized for now, but the crack in the Tianji Record remains. What are you planning to do next?" Chen Ji suppressed his emotions, his gaze regaining its sharpness: "Wait." His voice returned to its usual calm. "Since Ling Yuan has made his move, he will certainly move again. Let me see what this old Sect Master... truly wants." Morning light grew brighter, illuminating his pale yet determined features. And that blurry prophecy about Su Qingyao was like a thorn, deeply embedded in the softest corner of his heart.

Su Qingyao gazed at his composed analytical demeanor and silently vowed—no matter what the future held, she would never let him face it alone. As for Ye Qing, she glanced at Chen Ji with a contemplative look; the demonic path saint's intuition told her this man was far more dangerous than he appeared, yet also far more... inviting to be close to. The fates of these three people had been thoroughly intertwined in this night, and on the chessboard that enveloped the world, a new game was about to unfold.

Just at this moment, the Tianji Record within the Mental Sea suddenly trembled slightly. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul transmitted a weak message: "Lad... just now this old man sensed that the reason your backlash is so severe is not only because you rewrote causality—but more importantly, when you rewrote fate, someone took the opportunity to siphon away a portion of your Heavenly Fate Power." Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply: "Who?" Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, his voice carrying a trace of solemnity: "This old man isn't certain, but that aura... shares the same origin as the Heavenly Eye."

Chen Ji's heart sank. Someone was taking advantage of the chaos—during the very moment he used the power of fate-writing, some hidden enemy quietly took a portion of the Heavenly Fate Power that should have been his burden to bear, then framed him, causing the backlash to come even more violently. What did this mean? It meant that this chess player was not only setting up schemes for the world, but also coveting his Tianji Record. He took a deep breath, suppressing the surging thoughts. Regardless, the priority was to clarify the truth behind that vague prophecy—what did the scene of Su Qingyao's bloodied face falling into his arms actually signify?

The morning breeze brushed past the cave dwelling, carrying a chill. Chen Ji stood in place, his gaze deep and profound as an abyss. The backlash of Heavenly Fate, Ling Yuan's watching eyes, the Demonic Path's ambitions, the Heavenly Eye's coveting—all the clues pointed in the same direction: that chessboard that had loomed over him for twenty years was accelerating its closure. And he had to find a way to break the game before the next backlash arrived. Su Qingyao gazed at his profile, then suddenly reached out and gently grasped his fingers. Her palm was warm, carrying a silent comfort. Chen Ji lowered his head to look at that hand, a faint smile briefly appearing at the corner of his mouth: "Let's go, the show isn't over yet." he said softly, "The following plot... will be even more spectacular."
